title: Audit log viewer commands
goal: Let workspace admins read and export the audit log from the CLI, with filters, safe file output and clear messages when the plan or role does not allow it.
scope_in: `centcom audit list [--workspace wsp_..] [--actor <id>] [--action <name>] [--from <time>] [--to <time>] [--limit n] [--json]` over GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/audit with cursor pagination (`--limit` 1..200, default 50) and stable ordering.

`centcom audit export --format csv|json [--from] [--to] [--actor] [--action] [--out <file>] [--wait] [--force]`: POST .../audit/exports (Idempotency-Key), then poll GET .../audit/exports/{exp} (2 s growing to 10 s, give up after 5 min) and stream the download to a file.
Time parsing: RFC 3339 or relative (`24h`, `7d`); converted to UTC with millisecond precision; invalid input rejected locally.
Output: human table (time, actor, action, target, outcome) with control characters stripped, and `--json` passthrough; exit code 4 when no events match (optional) else 0.
Pre-checks and messages: `audit_log_days == 0` (feature off) from entitlements, `audit:read` scope and admin+ role hints; mapped `forbidden`.
scope_out: Writing audit events (server) and audit viewer UI (lane C091).
HTTP plumbing/auth: lanes C051, C052. Entitlement cache: lane C064 (this lane reads entitlements once via the HTTP client only for the pre-check).
Log shipping or SIEM integration (webhooks lane C069 covers events delivery).
build_against: the mock backend (lane C007): REST from OpenAPI plus the WebSocket relay simulator, started in-process with `startMockBackend()` from @centcom/testkit; no real backend is needed. The mock serves a generated audit log (10 000 events with actors, actions, outcomes), supports the filters, pagination, export job lifecycle (pending, ready with a download URL, failed, expired) and the 403/entitlement paths.
interfaces: CLI: `centcom audit list [--workspace wsp_..] [--actor <id>] [--action <name>] [--from <time>] [--to <time>] [--limit n] [--json]`; `centcom audit export --format csv|json [--from] [--to] [--actor] [--action] [--out <file>] [--wait] [--force]`
`registerAuditCommands(program, deps: { http: HttpClient; io; clock; fs: FsLike; isTTY: boolean })`
`parseTimeFilter(input: string, now: Date): string /* RFC 3339 UTC ms */`
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failure, 2 auth required, 4 no matching events (list only)
acceptance: `audit list --limit 120` against the 10 000-event mock follows cursors until 120 rows are printed, sends `limit<=200` per request and never an offset; `--json` emits one JSON array of 120 events.

`--actor`, `--action`, `--from` and `--to` are forwarded as query filters; `--from 24h` resolves relative to the injected clock to an RFC 3339 `...Z` value with millisecond precision; `--from yesterday` is rejected locally with exit 1.

`audit export --format csv --wait --out a.csv` sends POST with an Idempotency-Key, polls at 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 10 s (cap) on the fake clock until `ready`, downloads to `a.csv` with mode 0600 and prints the byte count; a `failed` job exits 1 with its code.
An existing output file is not overwritten without `--force` (exit 1, file untouched); a partial download is deleted on failure and on SIGINT.
Polling gives up after 5 minutes with a message including the export id so the user can resume with `audit export --status <exp>`-style re-run (the id is printed on creation).
When entitlements report `audit_log_days: 0` the command exits 1 with the 'audit log is not part of your plan' message and makes no audit request; a 403 shows the admin+ hint.
Event fields from the server containing control or ANSI characters are stripped in table mode; JSON mode preserves data as received.
No bearer token, signed download URL or export URL appears in logs or error output.
tests: audit/list.test.ts: pagination, limits, filters, empty result exit code.
audit/time-filter.test.ts: RFC 3339, relative units, invalid inputs, DST-independent UTC.
audit/export.test.ts: job lifecycle with fake clock, force/overwrite, SIGINT cleanup, permissions.
guardrails: MUST NOT write export files with permissions broader than 0600 and MUST NOT overwrite existing files without `--force`.
MUST NOT log or print signed download URLs; stream the body directly to disk with a size/time bound (no unbounded memory buffering).
MUST NOT use offset pagination or fetch more than the requested `--limit` rows into memory.
MUST treat role and plan pre-checks as hints only; the server's 403 is authoritative and is shown as is.
MUST sanitise terminal output (strip control and escape sequences) for table mode.
failure_modes: Export job expires before download -> exit 1 with 'export expired, run again'; no partial file.
Network failure mid-download -> remove partial file, exit 1, suggest re-run (export id printed).
Large log (millions of rows) -> `list` stays bounded by `--limit`; `export` is the path for bulk data.
